answer: Sybils are cheap to open, so make leaving an identity expensive: an exit bond. Dissolving an alias requires a retirement bond that grows with the standing it earned from paid closes. Abandoning one forfeits that bond, so the karst of cheap identities collapses under its own weight: each new alias must either pay the exit price or keep working honestly. A mirror ledger records every paid close, and the rule is crystal-clear: cost(n) sums renewal fees across all closes, super-linear per alias and identical for any coalition, since pooled operators pay the same growing exit price per pseudonym.
